newsitem.title: USA: Enron calls for U.S. action on electricity.
newsitem.headline: Enron calls for U.S. action on electricity.

text.p: Action from the federal goverment on setting a deadline for retail electricity competition is "imperative," Enron Corp president Jeffrey Skilling said Thursday at a Senate Energy Committee workshop.

"There are few issues so national in scope. We are all connected to an electric grid that knows no state boundaries. Retail electric choice...demands a federal response," Enron, one of the world's largest integrated natural gas companies and the largest wholesale marketer of electricity in the U.S., said in a statement.
Nationwide competition would result in daily savings of around $200 million for homes and business, the company said.
"Monopoly utilities will parade before you what they believe are the horrible and intractable problems of ending their monopolies," Skilling said.
"Until you set a deadline, that's all they'll do. A deadline forces them to stop listing problems, and start listing solutions," he added.
